title: The Watch — Sc111: faces mashed flat against the glass pane (KeyAnim line art)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: The faces-on-glass gag is a layer trick: a translucent glass-pane prop (GB219Watch_Props_GlassPane_v001.fxg) sits on its own foreground 'glass' layer over the whole shot, and the characters — riding episode-specific mobility-scooter pose puppets — come up behind it and squash. For the first ~30 frames Gumball (top) and Darwin (below) are upright and worried with their palms on the glass; then the face comps flatten, cheeks balloon and features smear across the pane until both are pressed blobs (f43-68). This file is the KeyAnim export, so the render is pale line art with only accent colours (Gumball's ear, Darwin's legs) — the construction, not the finish, is what it teaches.
notes: Honest render state: the companion SWF is the KeyAnim pass — the contact sheet is pale line art with unfinished colour (white below the glass line) and the animator's red markup circles still visible on the squash contact points; ROUGH_Gumball (11 kf) and ROUGH_DARWIN (9 kf) shape layers ship inside the file.
The library also carries single-pose Gumball variants around the beat: BACKVIEW (8 kf), FLOPPED (9 kf) and FRONTVIEW (10 kf) puppets.
The scooter is split into SCOOTER_FRONT_SC111_A and SCOOTER_BEHIND_SC111_A layers that sandwich the riders.
Face comps hold 3,868 kf vs 581 body kf: the squash lives in the dedicated scooter-puppet face comps (scooter GB mouth comp 457 kf).
